Team — forwarding first alert from on-call. Acme reports sustained 5xx and timeouts for their dedicated capacity pool this morning starting ~07:50 PST. On-call indicates autoscaler did not spawn new nodes due to a config mismatch (min_nodes=0 for a reserved pool). We're seeing cluster saturation triggered by a large offline batch job from the customer that exceeded expected concurrency.

- Dylan: can you confirm whether the autoscaler config change was pushed during last week's rollout?
- Aditya: please pull the admissions/eviction logs for the us-west-2 dedicated pool and attach anything that looks like saturation thresholds being hit.
- Lauren: please draft an initial customer-facing status update and list mitigation steps we took.

I will coordinate with CS and include ACME contacts once we have an accurate timeline. I attached the initial diagnostics that on-call dropped into the ticket.

Date: 2026-02-09T09:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity incident — immediate update

Jack — thanks for the quick report and for sharing the job IDs. Wanted to give you an early, transparent update while we continue triage.

What happened (short): between ~07:50-08:25 PST our us-west-2 dedicated GPU pool serving your account experienced cluster saturation and elevated 5xx rates. A large offline batch inference job submitted from Acme exceeded the concurrency envelope we expected and the autoscaler did not kick in because a recent configuration change set minimum nodes to 0 for that reserved pool. This combination allowed CPU/GPU scheduling contention to spike and requests to queue and time out.

What we did (mitigation):
- Immediately throttled and paused background batch jobs originating from Acme to reduce load (07:55 PST).
- Temporarily reconfigured the pool to enforce min_nodes=2 while we stabilized (08:02 PST).
- Redeployed the autoscaler with a hotfix to ignore min_nodes=0 for reserved pools and rebuilt pod evictions (08:14 PST).
- Replayed warm prefixes for hot sessions to refill caches and reduce tokenization latency (08:20 PST).

Current status: traffic normalized for most production routes by 08:30 PST. Our monitoring shows residual error spikes for some long-tail logs; we continue 1:1 monitoring and will keep you posted.

Next steps:
- We will provide a full timeline and postmortem by EOD tomorrow (Feb 10).
- Offer: we are prepared to credit impacted tokens for the window and discuss a permanent autoscaler guardrail for your Dedicated pools.
- A postmortem call is scheduled for Fri Feb 12 at 09:00 PST if that works for you — invite below.

Apologies for the impact. We're treating this as high priority and will share the root cause and corrective actions. If you want an immediate bridge, I can pull Lauren and Dylan onto a call.

Best,
Monica
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Subject: DRAFT Postmortem — Dedicated GPU pool saturation (us-west-2)

Folks — drafting the postmortem for review before we send to Acme tomorrow. Key points below and attached more detailed logs and an updated runbook. Please review inline and add missing timeline items.

Summary: On 2026-02-09 between 07:50-08:25 PST the Acme dedicated pool in us-west-2 hit sustained GPU/CPU scheduling contention due to an unexpected high-concurrency batch job from the customer combined with an autoscaler configuration that allowed min_nodes=0 for a reserved pool. Autoscaler scale-up thresholds were not reached because the controller interpreted min_nodes=0 as outside reserved pool guardrails.

Impact: Production requests returned 5xx/timeouts for approx 38 minutes for affected routes; we estimate ~1.2M tokens impacted across user-facing and background workloads. Customer-facing flows saw a spike in support volume.

Root cause: three contributing factors
- Configuration change deployed during a recent autoscaling roll (PR #874) permitted min_nodes=0 for reserved pools (human error + missing validation).
- No hard guardrail in the autoscaler to enforce a minimum baseline for dedicated/reserved pools.
- Lack of early throttling for large batch jobs originating from customer-managed orchestration.

Immediate remediation (already done):
- Reverted the config and enforced min_nodes=2 for all reserved pools (done 08:02 PST).
- Hotfix to the autoscaler controller to ignore min_nodes=0 for reserved pools (deployed 08:14 PST).
- Temporarily blocked non-critical batch job queueing for Acme and resumed after stabilization (07:55-08:22 PST).

Longer term action items (owners + ETA):
- Autoscaler validation rule to reject min_nodes<1 for reserved pools (owner: Dylan Brooks, ETA: 2026-02-17).
- Admission webhook to flag high-concurrency jobs for review (owner: Aditya Rao, ETA: 2026-02-28).
- Customer-facing guardrail: limit simultaneous background batch concurrency by default and surface opt-in for higher concurrency (owner: Lauren Bishop, ETA: 2026-03-05).
- Billing/credits calculation and automated token-impact export for customers (owner: Monica Patel, ETA: 2026-02-13).

Attachments: runbook_revision_v2.pdf, diagnostics_log_20260209.txt

Please suggest edits by EOD; I will finalize and send the external postmortem by 2026-02-11. Also linking the support ticket: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1421

-Aditya
Senior Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-02-11T16:42:00Z
Subject: External postmortem & next steps — Dedicated GPU pool saturation (us-west-2)

Jack — attached is the final postmortem and the runbook excerpt with the autoscaler validation changes. Key takeaways:
- Root cause: autoscaler configuration allowed min_nodes=0 for a reserved pool combined with an unthrottled large batch job from Acme.
- Corrective actions: enforced min_nodes>=1 for reserved pools, autoscaler controller hotfix, new admission checks for high-concurrency batch submissions.
- Customer impact: we estimate ~1.2M tokens affected across user paths; we will credit impacted tokens and apply a service credit for SLA window per our discussion.

Planned follow-ups:
- Credits: Monica will send a token-impact export and invoice credit by 2026-02-13. (owner: Monica Patel)
- Technical follow-ups: Dylan and Aditya will deliver the autoscaler validation rule and admission webhook. (owners: Dylan Brooks, Aditya Rao)
- Postmortem call: Fri Feb 12, 09:00 PST — calendar invite link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=postmortem-acme-20260212

If acceptable, we'll file a formal change to your Dedicated capacity plan to include an explicit baseline min_nodes and an optional pre-commit review for high-concurrency jobs. Appreciate the partnership here and apologies again for the disruption — we'll follow up with credits and a more formal SLA remediation offer.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
